reason: The sources provide over 15 distinct claims supported by multiple independent sites, easily supporting a compelling 45-second script about Pluto's discovery, demotion, and physical traits.
story: In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto at Lowell Observatory, and the world celebrated the addition of a ninth planet to our solar system. Suggested by eleven-year-old Venetia Burney, the name Pluto honored the Roman god of the underworld. For decades Pluto captured human imagination, but astronomers gradually realized how unusual it was. Pluto is smaller in diameter than Earth's Moon and follows a highly tilted, 248-year elliptical orbit that actually brought it closer to the Sun than Neptune between 1979 and 1999. In 2006, the International Astronomical Union redefined what constitutes a planet. Because Pluto resides in the Kuiper belt and has not cleared its orbital neighborhood of other debris, it was reclassified as a dwarf planet. In July 2015, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft completed the first close flyby, revealing nitrogen glaciers, floating water-ice mountains, and five distinct moons orbiting this tiny world.
angle: Despite reigning as the solar system's ninth planet for 76 years, Pluto is smaller in diameter than Earth's Moon and was demoted after failing to clear its orbital path.

claims.claim: Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto in 1930 at the Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona.
Eleven-year-old English schoolgirl Venetia Burney suggested the name Pluto for the newly discovered world.
Pluto was named after the Roman god of the underworld.
Pluto was initially hailed and officially classified as the solar system's ninth planet.
In 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.
Pluto was demoted because it failed the IAU requirement to clear the neighborhood around its orbit.
NASA's New Horizons spacecraft performed the first close flyby of Pluto on July 14, 2015.
Charon is Pluto's largest moon, measuring roughly half the diameter of Pluto itself.
Pluto has five known moons: Charon, Styx, Nix, Kerberos, and Hydra.
Pluto and Charon are mutually tidally locked, forcing them to always show the same face to each other.
Pluto takes approximately 248 Earth years to complete one orbit around the Sun.
From 1979 to 1999, Pluto's eccentric orbit brought it closer to the Sun than Neptune.
Pluto's orbit is tilted more than 17 degrees out of the orbital plane of the solar system.
Pluto is smaller in diameter than Earth's Moon.
Pluto's thin atmosphere is composed primarily of nitrogen, with trace amounts of methane and carbon monoxide.
The astronomical symbol for Pluto (PL) is a monogram that honors observatory founder Percival Lowell.

disputed: Origin of Disney's Pluto character: One account states Walt Disney was inspired by the planet's discovery in 1930, while another notes animator Ben Sharpsteen could not confirm the link. A script should attribute this as 'according to popular accounts' or omit it.

Atmospheric pressure trend post-2015: Ground occultations in 2019/2021 suggested a 20% drop in atmospheric pressure, whereas a 2026 study indicated pressure remained stable until 2022 before dropping. A script should leave out exact year-by-year pressure metrics.

Quasi-satellite classification of 15810 Arawn: Some astronomers calculate it as a quasi-satellite of Pluto, while others argue its orbit is controlled primarily by Neptune. A script should omit Arawn.
